opus-h1-014-a1.description: Steps 113-114 and the Canopy painted the operator-variable link counter 32 on the words of the moved wh-phrase: Which₃₂ cake₃₂. Test input for tests/heldoutLabelDefects.test.mjs.
opus-h1-014-a1.sentence: Which cake did Hana say that her brother thought the children had eaten?

derivationStages.statement: The wh-phrase 'which cake' is built as a DP.
derivationStages.stageRecord: The noun 'cake' projects through N' to NP. The wh-determiner 'which' takes that NP as its complement, forming D' and then DP. The [+wh] feature of 'which' percolates to the whole DP. This is why the full phrase, and not just the determiner, will later be the target of wh-movement. The first relation records this percolation from the determiner head to its maximal projection.

derivationStages.statement: The participle 'eaten' takes the wh-DP as its object.
derivationStages.stageRecord: The participle 'eaten' merges with the wh-DP as its complement, forming V' and then VP. This is the D-structure position where the DP's thematic role is determined. The first relation records that 'eaten' assigns the Theme role to the wh-DP, which it governs as its sister. The second relation records that 'eaten', as a transitive verb, assigns accusative Case to the same DP under government.

derivationStages.statement: The perfect auxiliary 'had' takes the participial VP as its complement.
derivationStages.stageRecord: The perfect auxiliary 'had' is generated as a verbal head. It merges with the VP headed by 'eaten', forming V' and VP. The relation records that perfect 'have' selects a complement VP headed by a past participle. This selection is why 'eat' surfaces as 'eaten'.

derivationStages.statement: The lowest finite Infl merges with the auxiliary VP.
derivationStages.stageRecord: An abstract finite Infl head carrying past tense and agreement merges with the VP headed by 'had'. It projects I' and an IP whose specifier is not yet filled. The relation records the tense and finiteness specification of this Infl. These features are what the auxiliary will associate with.

derivationStages.statement: The auxiliary 'had' raises from V to Infl.
derivationStages.stageRecord: English aspectual auxiliaries raise to Infl rather than being lowered onto. So 'had' moves out of its VP head position and adjoins to the abstract Infl. This forms a complex Infl head and leaves a silent trace in the auxiliary's base V position. The relation records this V-to-I head movement. It links the moved auxiliary, its trace and the Infl it adjoins to, and the auxiliary thereby carries the past tense of the clause.

derivationStages.statement: The subject 'the children' is merged in Spec-IP of the lowest clause.
derivationStages.stageRecord: The DP 'the children' is built and merged as the specifier of the lowest IP, completing that clause. The first relation records that the finite Infl, which governs its specifier, assigns nominative Case to this DP. The second relation records that the predicate headed by 'eaten' assigns its external Agent role to the subject. The third relation records Spec-head agreement between Infl and the plural third-person subject.

derivationStages.statement: A null C heads the lowest clause, and the wh-DP moves to its specifier.
derivationStages.stageRecord: A null non-interrogative complementizer merges with the lowest IP, projecting C' and CP. Because Subjacency forbids crossing two bounding nodes in one step, the wh-DP must move successive-cyclically. Its first step goes from object position to this Spec-CP, crossing only one IP. It leaves a silent trace in object position. The first relation records this A-bar movement, linking the moved DP to its trace. The second relation records that the object trace satisfies the Empty Category Principle by being lexically governed by 'eaten'.

derivationStages.statement: The verb 'thought' takes the lowest CP as its complement.
derivationStages.stageRecord: The verb 'thought' merges with the lowest CP, forming V' and VP. The relation records that 'thought' assigns its internal propositional role to that clausal complement, which it governs.

derivationStages.statement: The middle finite Infl merges, and its tense affix hops onto 'thought'.
derivationStages.stageRecord: An abstract past-tense finite Infl merges with the VP headed by 'thought', projecting I' and IP. Lexical verbs do not raise to Infl in English. Since 'thought' is adjacent to Infl, the tense affix lowers onto it instead, giving the past form. The first relation records the tense specification of this Infl. The second relation records affix hopping from the Infl to the verb 'thought'.

derivationStages.statement: The subject 'her brother' is merged in Spec-IP of the middle clause.
derivationStages.stageRecord: The DP 'her brother' is built, with the possessive pronoun as its determiner, and merged as the specifier of the middle IP. The first relation records nominative Case assigned to this DP by the finite Infl that governs it. The second relation records that 'thought' assigns its external Experiencer role to this subject. The third relation records Spec-head agreement in third person singular between Infl and the subject.

derivationStages.statement: The complementizer 'that' heads the middle clause, and the wh-DP moves to its specifier.
derivationStages.stageRecord: The overt complementizer 'that' merges with the middle IP, projecting C' and CP. The wh-DP then takes its second successive-cyclic step, from the lowest Spec-CP to this Spec-CP. It leaves an intermediate trace behind. This extraction is licit despite overt 'that' because the chain originates in object position, so no that-trace configuration arises. The first relation records this movement step, linking the moved DP to the intermediate trace. The second relation records that the step obeys Subjacency because it crosses only the middle IP as a bounding node.

derivationStages.statement: The verb 'say' takes the 'that'-clause as its complement.
derivationStages.stageRecord: The bare verb 'say' merges with the 'that'-CP, forming V' and VP. The relation records that 'say' assigns its internal propositional role to that clausal complement, which it governs.

derivationStages.statement: The matrix finite Infl merges with the VP headed by 'say'.
derivationStages.stageRecord: An abstract past-tense finite Infl merges with the VP headed by 'say', projecting I' and IP. Its affix is not lowered onto 'say', because this Infl will raise to C. The relation records the tense specification of the matrix Infl.

derivationStages.statement: The subject 'Hana' is merged in matrix Spec-IP.
derivationStages.stageRecord: The proper name 'Hana' projects to NP and merges as the specifier of the matrix IP. The first relation records nominative Case assigned to it by the governing finite Infl. The second relation records that 'say' assigns its external Agent role to it. The third relation records third-person singular Spec-head agreement with Infl.

derivationStages.statement: A null interrogative C heads the matrix clause.
derivationStages.stageRecord: A null complementizer bearing [+wh, +Q] merges with the matrix IP, projecting C' and a CP with an empty specifier. The relation records that this head types the whole sentence as a direct wh-question. That typing is what triggers inversion and attracts the wh-phrase to the matrix clause.

derivationStages.statement: The matrix Infl raises to C (subject-auxiliary inversion).
derivationStages.stageRecord: Matrix interrogative C attracts Infl, so the matrix Infl moves out of its head position and adjoins to C. It leaves a trace in Infl and ends up to the left of the subject 'Hana'. The relation records this I-to-C head movement, linking the moved Infl, its trace and the C it adjoins to.

derivationStages.statement: Do-support spells out the stranded past tense as 'did'.
derivationStages.stageRecord: After inversion, the past-tense affix in C is separated from 'say' by the subject 'Hana'. The adjacency required for affix hopping fails, and the affix cannot lower. To rescue the stranded affix, the dummy auxiliary 'do' is inserted under the raised Infl, which is now pronounced as 'did'. The relation records this do-support on the raised Infl.

derivationStages.statement: The wh-DP moves to matrix Spec-CP, completing the A-bar chain.
derivationStages.stageRecord: The wh-DP takes its final step, from the 'that'-clause's Spec-CP to matrix Spec-CP, leaving a third trace. The first relation records this movement step between the moved DP and the new trace. The second relation records that this step crosses only the matrix IP as a bounding node, so it obeys Subjacency. The third relation records Spec-head wh-agreement between the wh-DP and interrogative C, satisfying the wh-criterion. The fourth relation records the full A-bar chain, headed by the wh-DP and linking it through both intermediate traces to the object trace. The fifth relation records that the wh-DP, as an operator, binds the Case-marked object trace, which is interpreted as a variable.

sol-h1-070-a1.description: From step 56 the relative trace rop showed i twice: its theta letter and the operator-variable binding letter, which the allocator gives the same chain. Test input for tests/heldoutLabelDefects.test.mjs.
sol-h1-070-a1.sentence: 昨日駅の前で会った女の人が、来週から私の会社で働くそうだ。

derivationStages.statement: Build the relative clause with an unexpressed subject and an oblique relative operator: someone met the woman yesterday in front of the station.
derivationStages.stageRecord: 会う selects a meeting partner bearing inherent dative case; the silent oblique operator occupies that argument position and receives the co-participant role. The referential null subject pro receives the external participant role; its identity is supplied by context and need not be the speaker. The genitive-marked 駅 restricts 前, yielding the location 駅の前で. This locative modifies the meeting event, while 昨日 supplies its time. Past I is realized as た following the verbal stem 会っ and licenses the null subject's nominative case. A silent relative C completes the clause, but its operator has not yet moved.

derivationStages.statement: Form an oblique relative chain and attach the relative clause to 女の人.
derivationStages.stageRecord: The oblique operator moves from the complement of 会う to Spec-CP, leaving a silent KP trace in the position already assigned the meeting-partner role and dative case. The operator locally A-bar-binds that trace; the chain receives only the single role assigned at its source. This is pied-piping of an abstract oblique phrase, not overt stranding of に. Independently, の marks 女 as a nominal restrictor of 人, producing 女の人. The completed relative CP adjoins to that nominal, identifying the woman with the meeting partner rather than the null subject. Thus the contextual null subject met the woman.

values.licensing: the trace is lexically governed by 会う and locally A-bar-bound by the operator

values.headInterpretation: the woman is the meeting co-participant represented by the oblique chain

derivationStages.statement: Build the reported proposition: the woman will work at my company starting next week.
derivationStages.stageRecord: The relative-modified nominal combines with が and occupies Spec-IP as the subject of 働く. 働く assigns this subject the worker role, and finite nonpast I licenses its nominative case, overtly marked by が. 来週から attaches as a temporal-onset adjunct to the working predicate. 私の restricts 会社 through genitive の, and 私の会社で supplies the workplace. The overt verb 働く carries its ordinary nonpast form; the separate abstract I has no independent pronunciation. A silent declarative C closes the proposition that the hearsay expression will select.

values.interpretation: the company associated with the speaker

derivationStages.statement: Complete the hearsay sentence, with the woman interpreted as the person whom the contextual subject met.
derivationStages.stageRecord: Hearsay そう selects the completed finite proposition and takes scope over the woman's working at the speaker's company starting next week. Its position after the plain nonpast form 働く identifies the hearsay construction, not the appearance construction, which would require 働きそうだ. The evidential projection combines with copular だ; silent nonpast I and declarative C close the impersonal reporting shell, without introducing another referential subject. The subject marked が remains inside the reported proposition. The resulting interpretation is approximately: 'I hear that the woman whom someone contextually understood met yesterday in front of the station will work at my company starting next week.'

values.scope: the complete proposition about the woman's future employment

sol-h1-070-a2.description: The second analysis of the same run, with the same doubled letter on rop from step 56. Test input for tests/heldoutLabelDefects.test.mjs.
sol-h1-070-a2.sentence: 昨日駅の前で会った女の人が、来週から私の会社で働くそうだ。

derivationStages.statement: Build the alternative relative clause with a subject operator: the woman met an unexpressed person yesterday in front of the station.
derivationStages.stageRecord: 会う assigns its inherent-dative complement pro the meeting co-participant role. This null complement denotes a contextually understood person. The silent relative operator is instead generated as the subject in Spec-IP and receives the external meeting-participant role. The genitive-marked 駅 restricts 前, giving 駅の前で; that PP locates the meeting, and 昨日 supplies its time. Past I is pronounced た after 会っ and licenses nominative case on the subject operator. A silent relative C completes the clause before operator movement. Unlike the other reading, the future worker is the subject of 会った, not its oblique argument.

derivationStages.statement: Form a subject relative chain and identify its participant with 女の人.
derivationStages.stageRecord: The subject operator moves from Spec-IP to Spec-CP, leaving a nominative NP trace in its original subject position. The operator locally A-bar-binds the trace, whose subject position is properly governed by finite I in the selected GB analysis; no overt complementizer intervenes. The chain retains the single external role assigned by 会う. Genitive の makes 女 a classificatory restrictor of 人. The relative CP adjoins to the resulting 女の人 nominal, identifying the woman with the relative subject. The dative pro remains a distinct, contextually interpreted meeting partner.

values.licensing: the subject trace is properly governed by finite I and locally A-bar-bound by the operator

values.headInterpretation: the woman is the subject participant represented by the nominative chain

derivationStages.statement: Build the reported employment proposition with the subject-relative nominal as its nominative subject.
derivationStages.stageRecord: The relative-modified 女の人 combines with が and occupies Spec-IP of the employment clause. 働く assigns it the worker role, and finite nonpast I licenses nominative case, expressed by が. 来週から modifies the working event with a starting boundary next week. Genitive の relates 私 to 会社, and 私の会社で supplies the workplace. 働く is the overt nonpast verb form, while abstract I remains unpronounced. A silent declarative C closes this proposition. The same woman is therefore the subject participant in the earlier meeting and the worker in the reported future event.

values.interpretation: the company associated with the speaker

derivationStages.statement: Complete the hearsay sentence with the woman interpreted as the subject of the relative clause.
derivationStages.stageRecord: Hearsay そう selects the completed employment proposition and takes scope over it. The plain form 働く before そう establishes hearsay rather than appearance; appearance would require 働きそうだ. Copular だ takes the evidential projection as its complement, and silent nonpast I and declarative C complete the impersonal reporting shell. No additional referential subject is introduced: が belongs to the worker inside the reported proposition. On this reading the sentence means approximately: 'I hear that the woman who met someone contextually understood yesterday in front of the station will work at my company starting next week.' The identity of that unexpressed meeting partner is contextual rather than a further structural ambiguity.

values.scope: the complete proposition about the woman's future employment

sol-h1-038-a1.description: Steps 37-38 painted two identical Agent theta plaques on higherVbar: the stage-2 theta claim and the stage-4 chain claim restating thetaRole Agent for the trace of the same chain. Test input for tests/heldoutLabelDefects.test.mjs.

derivationStages.statement: Construct the Marathi nominal expressions and the lexical heads for the head-final clause.
derivationStages.stageRecord: सीताने is projected as an NP headed by the inflected proper noun; its ergative ending remains inside the lexical terminal rather than being represented as a separate word. The object दोन पत्रे is an NP with the numeral phrase दोन in its specifier and पत्रे as its nominal head. The numeral quantifies the letters, establishing cardinality two. The subject has feminine singular features, whereas the object has neuter plural features. काल is projected as an adverbial phrase. लिहिली is introduced as the overt perfective verb, and a silent finite I supplies the clause's past-tense and perfective specifications. In this analysis, inflection is realized on the lexical verb without requiring syntactic V-to-I movement.

derivationStages.statement: Build the head-final VP and establish its thematic and temporal dependencies.
derivationStages.stageRecord: The object दोन पत्रे combines to the left of लिहिली under V′. The verb governs this complement and assigns it the Theme role. काल then adjoins to V′ as a temporal modifier of the writing event. Finally, सीताने occupies the VP-internal subject position and receives the Agent role from the verbal predicate. This places the arguments in their theta-positions before any subject movement. The temporal adverb is interpreted as yesterday in combination with the past perfective clause, not as a separate tomorrow reading.

derivationStages.statement: Project finite IP and license the ergative subject, unmarked object, and object agreement.
derivationStages.stageRecord: The VP combines with silent, clause-final I to form I′ and IP; Spec-IP is not yet occupied. I establishes a finite past-perfective interpretation for the verbal predicate. In the GB-style analysis of Marathi ergativity adopted here, the transitive perfective predicate licenses inherent ergative Case on सीताने, overtly expressed by ने. Finite I licenses unmarked structural nominative Case on the object दोन पत्रे through the verbal domain, while V remains its local governor. Because the subject is ergative, the unmarked object controls the finite predicate's agreement: the neuter plural features of पत्रे determine the neuter plural form लिहिली. These agreement and tense dependencies are realized on the verb already present in V; they do not introduce an additional pronounced auxiliary.

derivationStages.statement: Raise the ergative subject to Spec-IP and complete the surface clause.
derivationStages.stageRecord: सीताने moves from the previously established Spec-VP position to Spec-IP, leaving a silent NP trace in its original theta-position. This is A-movement satisfying the finite clause's subject-position requirement, not movement to obtain nominative Case: the subject retains its inherent ergative Case. The raised NP c-commands and antecedent-governs its trace, forming a single Agent chain whose thematic position remains inside VP. Neither the object nor काल moves. With silent I and the subject trace unpronounced, the completed head-final structure yields सीताने काल दोन पत्रे लिहिली, meaning that Sita wrote two letters yesterday.

opus-h1-030-a1.description: The leaf i1 labelled I with the word i painted only i: the category label was dropped because the label equals the word apart from case. Test input for tests/heldoutLabelDefects.test.mjs.
opus-h1-030-a1.sentence: Nā Hēmi te whare i hanga.

derivationStages.statement: The lexical building blocks are assembled: the patient DP 'te whare', the agent PP 'nā Hēmi', and the verb 'hanga'.
derivationStages.stageRecord: Three separate syntactic objects are formed. The determiner 'te' takes the NP 'whare' as its complement, giving the DP 'te whare'. The preposition 'nā' takes the proper-name NP 'Hēmi', giving the PP 'nā Hēmi'. The verb 'hanga' stands alone as a bare head, waiting for its arguments. Within the PP, 'nā' assigns inherent Case to 'Hēmi'. This is the agentive Case characteristic of the Māori actor-emphatic construction. It means the agent does not need any structural Case position later in the derivation.

derivationStages.statement: The VP is projected: 'hanga' takes 'te whare' as complement and the agent PP 'nā Hēmi' occupies Spec-VP.
derivationStages.stageRecord: First the verb 'hanga' merges with the DP 'te whare' to form V'. In doing so it assigns the Theme theta-role to 'te whare', the thing built. Next the PP 'nā Hēmi' merges as the specifier of the VP. The V' compositionally assigns it the Agent theta-role, the builder. All theta-roles of 'hanga' are now discharged inside the VP, as the Theta Criterion requires.

derivationStages.statement: The tense/aspect particle 'i' heads INFL and takes the VP as its complement.
derivationStages.stageRecord: The particle 'i' is inserted as the INFL head and merges with the VP, forming I'. It marks past/perfective tense-aspect and selects the VP as its complement. This places 'i' immediately before 'hanga', matching the surface string 'i hanga'.

derivationStages.statement: The patient 'te whare' A-moves to Spec-IP and receives nominative Case there.
derivationStages.stageRecord: In the actor-emphatic construction the verb form does not license structural Case on its object. The agent is already Case-marked by 'nā', so the theme 'te whare' is the only argument still needing structural Case. It therefore raises from complement of V to Spec-IP, leaving a coindexed trace in object position. The landing site forms the IP, which accounts for 'te whare' preceding 'i hanga'. This A-movement links the raised DP to its trace. In Spec-IP the DP is then assigned nominative Case by INFL, under specifier-head agreement.

derivationStages.statement: A null focus C selects the IP, and the agent PP 'nā Hēmi' A-bar-moves to Spec-CP as the emphasized constituent.
derivationStages.stageRecord: A phonologically null complementizer bearing a focus feature merges with the IP, forming C'. It selects the IP as its complement. The agent PP 'nā Hēmi' then moves from Spec-VP to Spec-CP, leaving a trace in Spec-VP. This is A-bar movement driven by focus: the construction emphasizes the actor, 'It was Hēmi who built the house'. It yields the sentence-initial position of 'nā Hēmi'. Finally, in Spec-CP the fronted PP stands in a specifier-head relation with the focus C, which licenses its focus interpretation. The resulting order is nā Hēmi, te whare, i hanga.

derivationStages.statement: The definite core of the object is built: the determiner le merges with the noun peek' ('dog').
derivationStages.stageRecord: The derivation starts bottom-up with the object 'the dog'. Yucatec definite reference uses a split determiner. The prenominal part le is a D head. It is externally merged with the nominal peek', and the result is labeled by D. No relation beyond this basic construction is claimed yet.

derivationStages.statement: The deictic enclitic o' merges with the determiner phrase, completing the discontinuous determiner le ... o'.
derivationStages.stageRecord: The terminal deictic o' is merged as a separate head taking the le-phrase as its complement. As an enclitic, it is linearized at the right edge of the nominal, which gives le peek'o'. This Merge also sets up a concord relation between the deictic head and the determiner le. That relation is what licenses the circumfixal le ... o' pattern, and its deictic value is distal/default.

derivationStages.statement: The verbal root il ('see') merges with the object nominal, forming VP.
derivationStages.stageRecord: The transitive root il is merged with the completed object le peek'o' as its complement. This first Merge discharges the root's internal theta role, assigning Theme to the object nominal.

derivationStages.statement: Transitive v, spelled out as the completive status suffix -aj, merges with VP and Agrees with the object.
derivationStages.stageRecord: The transitive light verb is merged with VP. In the completive transitive it surfaces as the status suffix -aj. On Merge, v probes its c-command domain and finds the object nominal. Agree values v's features as third person singular and licenses the object with absolutive case. The third-singular Set B exponent is null, which is why nothing overt marks the object on the verb.

derivationStages.statement: The root il head-moves to v, forming the complex verb stem il-aj.
derivationStages.stageRecord: The suffix -aj needs a verbal host, so the root il raises from its VP-internal position and adjoins to v. This forms the complex head il-aj, with the root to the left of the suffix. The raised root keeps its identity at the landing site. Its VP-internal source is left as an unpronounced copy of the same object. This movement is recorded as a separate stage after v's Merge because it depends on v being present.

derivationStages.statement: A null first-person pronoun merges as the external argument in the specifier of vP.
derivationStages.stageRecord: Yucatec freely drops pronominal subjects, so the subject 'I' is a silent pro. It is externally merged with the v-projection and becomes its specifier. The complex verb stem il-aj assigns it the external theta role. For a perception verb like 'see', that role is Experiencer.

derivationStages.statement: The ergative agreement head inw merges above vP and Agrees with the null subject.
derivationStages.stageRecord: A Set A (ergative) agreement head is merged with vP. Its prevocalic first-singular form is inw-; orthographically, its w is written on the following verb stem. It probes downward and finds the silent subject in the specifier of vP. Agree values it as first person singular, and the subject is licensed with ergative case. This agreement is the only overt trace of the dropped subject.

derivationStages.statement: The completive aspect head t merges at the top of the clause, completing 'Tin wilaj le peek'o''.
derivationStages.stageRecord: The completive aspect head t- is merged with the ergative phrase and projects the clause. Completive aspect requires the matching status suffix on the transitive verb. This aspect head is therefore in a concord relation with v, which is spelled out as -aj. Linearizing the result gives t, inw, the raised il, -aj, then le peek' o'. The subject and the lower root copy are silent, so the string is 'Tin wilaj le peek'o''.

sol-c1-013-a1.sentence: Ik weet dat Jan het boek wil kopen.

derivationStages.statement: Build the head-final lexical predicate het boek kopen.
derivationStages.stageRecord: Merge het with boek to form the definite object, then merge that object to the left of kopen. The resulting object–verb order supplies the lexical core of the Dutch infinitival predicate. Kopen assigns its Theme role to het boek. Projection labels identify the projecting head without introducing bar-level categories.

derivationStages.statement: Introduce Jan as the embedded predicate's external argument.
derivationStages.stageRecord: Merge a silent verbalizing head above the lexical predicate, maintaining head-final order, and externally merge Jan at its edge. The verbalizing head introduces Jan as the Agent of buying. Jan is therefore initially interpreted inside the predicate that will be selected by the restructuring modal.

derivationStages.statement: Raise kopen to the embedded verbalizing head.
derivationStages.stageRecord: Move kopen from its established complement position to the silent verbalizing head, adjoining it on the left. Leave an unpronounced V trace in the lexical predicate. This local step creates the complex verbal head that can subsequently raise into the modal cluster without skipping the intervening verbalizing head.

derivationStages.statement: Merge finite modal wil above the embedded predicate.
derivationStages.stageRecord: Merge wil as a head-final finite modal T selecting the verbal predicate. On this restructuring analysis, wil introduces no separate infinitival CP or independently licensed infinitival subject; its volitional interpretation is oriented toward Jan, the buying predicate's subject. Establish agreement between wil and the still-low Jan, licensing nominative Case and present-tense third-person singular inflection.

derivationStages.statement: Form wil kopen and raise Jan to the embedded subject position.
derivationStages.stageRecord: First raise the complex verbal head containing kopen from the verbalizing-head position and right-adjoin it to wil. This verb-cluster operation produces the attested modal–infinitive order wil kopen while leaving het boek in its original preverbal object position. An unpronounced verbal-head trace marks the vacated position. Then internally merge Jan at the edge of T, leaving an unpronounced subject trace in the verbal predicate. These operations yield Jan het boek wil kopen.

values.operation: right adjunction to the finite modal

derivationStages.statement: Introduce the embedded declarative complementizer dat.
derivationStages.stageRecord: Merge dat to the left of the completed finite T projection. Dat selects the finite declarative clause and supplies its overt complementizer position. No movement of the embedded finite cluster to C is triggered here, so the complement retains Jan het boek wil kopen after dat.

derivationStages.statement: Build the matrix predicate and introduce Ik.
derivationStages.stageRecord: Merge the dat clause as the complement of weet, initially to its left in the head-final matrix verbal domain. Weet selects this clause as its factive propositional content. Merge a silent matrix verbalizing head and then Ik at its edge; this head introduces Ik as the Experiencer of knowing.

derivationStages.statement: Raise weet to the matrix verbalizing head.
derivationStages.stageRecord: Move weet from the position following its clausal complement and left-adjoin it to the silent matrix verbalizing head. Leave an unpronounced V trace beside the complement. This establishes the first local step of the matrix head-movement chain that will ultimately place weet in the root V2 position.

derivationStages.statement: Merge matrix T and license the subject's finite features.
derivationStages.stageRecord: Merge a silent present-tense T above the matrix verbal domain. T agrees with Ik in its existing external-argument position, licensing nominative Case and first-person singular agreement. The finite form associated with this dependency is weet; the abstract T has no independently pronounced exponent.

derivationStages.statement: Raise the matrix verb to T and Ik to the T edge.
derivationStages.stageRecord: First move the complex matrix verbal head to T by left adjunction, leaving a silent verbal-head trace. This carries weet into the finite head without changing its pronunciation. Then raise Ik from its established external-argument position to the edge of T and leave a silent subject trace. The resulting T projection is the source for the root verb-second operations.

derivationStages.statement: Establish root C and move the finite matrix head into it.
derivationStages.stageRecord: Merge a silent root declarative C above the matrix T projection. Its verb-second requirement attracts the already formed finite T head containing weet. Left-adjoin that head to C and leave an unpronounced T trace. Weet now precedes the matrix T projection and its clausal complement; Ik remains at the T edge until the next step.

derivationStages.statement: Complete the subject-initial V2 clause Ik weet dat Jan het boek wil kopen.
derivationStages.stageRecord: Move Ik from its previously established T-edge position to the root C edge, leaving a second silent subject trace. This supplies the single preverbal constituent required by the root V2 structure, without imposing a contrastive-topic interpretation. The pronounced terminals now occur in exactly the input order: Ik weet dat Jan het boek wil kopen. The embedded subject and verb traces remain silent, as do the matrix subject and head-movement traces.
